name: Sea Monsters and Sky Dragons of the Deep Past
description: Ichthyosaurs, mosasaurs, pterosaurs and giant sharks: the great reptiles of the Mesozoic oceans and skies, and the whales and sharks that came after.

checkpoints.name: Armoured seas
checkpoints.note: Long before dinosaurs, the Devonian sea belonged to armoured fish like Dunkleosteus. The Permian-Triassic extinction cleared the oceans and made room for new rulers.

checkpoints.name: Reptiles return to the sea
checkpoints.note: In the Triassic, reptiles went back to the water. Ichthyosaurs, with dolphin-like bodies, spread through the oceans, until the Triassic-Jurassic extinction ended the period.

checkpoints.name: Jurassic oceans and skies
checkpoints.note: Plesiosaurs hunted in Jurassic seas, and Mary Anning found early skeletons at Lyme Regis. Pterosaurs such as Pterodactylus flew above, and Archaeopteryx shows how birds are related to dinosaurs.

checkpoints.name: Cretaceous giants
checkpoints.note: In the Cretaceous the Western Interior Seaway split North America, mosasaurs ruled the sea, Spinosaurus hunted in rivers and Quetzalcoatlus, a giant pterosaur, flew. The Chicxulub impact ended this world.

checkpoints.name: Giants of the new seas
checkpoints.note: After the extinction, new hunters filled the seas. Whales evolved from land mammals, and Basilosaurus was an early whale. The huge shark megalodon hunted until a few million years ago, while great whites and blue whales live on. On land, Titanoboa was a giant snake.
